cuts.title: Lean for biology · two-minute science cut

scenes.narration: Lean for biology is the foundation: mathematical claims with explicit assumptions and machine-checkable consequences.
scenes.headline: Lean for biology

scenes.narration: Formalize that knowledge, and new capabilities become possible: reusable constraints, compatible models, candidate designs and experiments that target the missing evidence.
scenes.headline: Formal claims make knowledge reusable

scenes.narration: Our test case is a fish that could glide, starting from zebrafish. Published fin-growth genetics and natural flying-fish measurements help frame the design.
scenes.headline: A demanding test case: a flying fish

scenes.narration: We formalized a fin-beam stiffness condition that bounds deflection. Lean compiled the theorem and rejected a corrupted law. Two computations reused a versioned mechanics claim; independent review preserved both the numerical checks and questions about biological relevance.
scenes.headline: A conditional theorem, compiled and tested

scenes.narration: The studio spans sequence candidates, bioelectric models, fin mechanics, aerodynamics and collective behavior. Each layer exposes equations, controls and evidence. Virtual instruments show model-specific predictions, not measurements.
scenes.headline: Virtual instruments across scales

scenes.narration: The ambition is a biological compiler: candidate DNA, a build plan and a validation strategy. Our current compiler checks linked artifacts and identifies unresolved interfaces.
scenes.headline: A biological compiler is an intended output

scenes.narration: Like AlphaFold predictions, computational candidates are hypotheses to test. We combine formal checks, numerical controls and observations, then use failures to guide the next experiment.
scenes.headline: Predictions need tests

scenes.narration: Through MCP, people and agents can contribute, challenge and reuse that work. The flying fish is one example. The larger goal is a shared, checkable foundation for engineering biology.
scenes.headline: Build a shared, checkable foundation
